summary: Router 0.27.0 on top of main with ADR-0082: at start the router checks its own view (/proc/self/mountinfo, owner and mode, effective capabilities) and reports the medium posture finding tls_files_changeable (TM-14, ADR-0083) when it could change or replace control_tls.cert or control_tls.key or a folder above them. The next step names /etc/skirnir-router/certs and /etc/skirnir-router/tls (read-only for the unit since ADR-0073 and ADR-0082), or keeping the files outside the router's writable folders. The check only reads /proc/self and stat results of the configured paths; it writes nothing, reads no certificate or key content, and router.py --posture leaves it out. Reviewed: process_view.py in full, its caller in app.main (runs before unreadable_files and the TLS context), the posture finding, CI wiring, the unit lines it relies on (router/skirnir-router.service on main) and the docs.

findings.evidence: ADR-0073 and ADR-0082 make only /etc/skirnir-router/certs and /etc/skirnir-router/tls read-only for the router unit (root without capabilities, ReadWritePaths=/etc/skirnir-router). A certificate or key in any other folder below the router's writable folders, or under a unit override without those lines, stays replaceable by a compromised router, and nothing reported it.
findings.resolution: The running router reports tls_files_changeable with the next step. It checks the file (writable mount plus owner, group or mode), every folder above it (rename or replace), mount points, sticky folders, symlink and target, CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE and CAP_FOWNER; an owner on a writable mount counts as writer because chmod needs only ownership. The self-test mirrors the current unit (certs and tls read-only): files there give no finding, files in another folder below /etc/skirnir-router do.

findings.evidence: Found in this review: changeable() walked up with `while entry != "/"`. control_tls accepts relative paths (no absolute-path check in config.py), and for a relative path the walk reaches "" where dirname("") is "", so the start-time check looped forever before the router listened. Trigger is the operator's configuration (control_tls is not editable in the web UI); impact is a router that does not start serving.
findings.resolution: The path is joined to the working directory, where the router opens it, and the walk ends when dirname returns its input. test_relative_path and test_walk_ends_without_absolute_path fail against the previous code (wrong verdict; thread still looping after 5 s) and pass now.

findings.evidence: A check that raised at start (stat of a path the process cannot reach, a dangling link) would stop the router before it serves.
findings.resolution: Paths are checked with lexists before any stat; a link target is only stat-ed when it exists; folders above an existing entry are reachable by construction. No try/except added (check_control_flow: 0 findings). Dangling links in read-only and writable folders are tested.

findings.evidence: The finding writes configured paths to the start log.
findings.resolution: Only the setting name and the configured path (as config.yaml holds it) are printed; no file content, owner or other path.

limitations: The Linux-only test of the running process's own view ran in CI (Ubuntu), not locally: the local WSL Python lacks aiohttp.
ACLs, security modules and immutable attributes are not read; they can only remove rights, so the check may over-report, never under-report.
A configured path with '..' through a symlink is walked after lexical normalisation as well as at its resolved target; the link swapped by such a '..' is judged only through the folders above it.
The finding only appears in the start log of the running router; router.py --posture cannot see the unit's view.
No end-to-end run on a real systemd unit for this change; the unit lines themselves were verified with systemd for ADR-0082.
